title: SEC-003: Add CSRF protection headers
description: API requests are made with auth headers but no CSRF token. If the backend requires or supports CSRF protection, the X-CSRF-Token header should be included. This task adds conditional CSRF token support based on backend verification.

context.current_pattern: Only includes Content-Type and Authorization headers
context.issue: Missing CSRF protection headers if backend requires them

acceptance_criteria: Verify with backend team if CSRF tokens are required or supported
If yes: Add X-CSRF-Token header to request headers
If no: Document decision and skip implementation
CSRF token should be read from meta tag: document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]')
Header is conditionally added only if CSRF token exists in DOM
All state-changing requests (POST, PUT, DELETE) include CSRF header
Requests without CSRF token in DOM still work (graceful fallback)

implementation_notes.csrf_token_source: Read from <meta name="csrf-token" content="..."> tag in HTML
implementation_notes.verification_step: Ask backend team: Do you require or support CSRF token validation?
implementation_notes.if_not_required: Document decision and mark as RESOLVED (skip implementation)

backend_verification: Contact backend team to confirm CSRF token requirement
Check if backend uses X-CSRF-Token header or different header name
Verify CSRF tokens are provided in meta tag or another source
unit_test: Mock meta tag with CSRF token
Test with missing meta tag; verify header is not added
Verify Authorization header still works with/without CSRF token
integration_test: Make POST/PUT/DELETE request with CSRF token
Verify backend accepts request with X-CSRF-Token header
Test without CSRF token (if backend allows)
Test with invalid CSRF token (should fail)

rollback_plan: git revert <commit-hash> — conditional header addition, safe to revert if not needed
notes: This task is CONDITIONAL on backend verification. It's marked HIGH in review but marked MEDIUM priority here because implementation depends on backend team confirmation. If backend doesn't require CSRF tokens, this can be skipped. If required, it's a security-critical fix.
